summary: Client-IP surface change splits session pin across canary and baseline during rolling promote
description: Issue summary: Over the last 6 hours BrightFields observed repeated mixed-model responses for the same tenant/session during our staged canary promote. Impact: Customer request traffic intermittently routed to baseline model (redwood-3b-v1) instead of pinned canary variant, impacting output consistency and evaluation metrics. Environment: Dedicated pool for BrightFields in us-west (prod).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightFields tenant api key against production endpoint for route /v1/complete with canonical multi-turn payload
2) Send 30 requests rapidly from the same client behind the customer's load balancer using varying outbound source IPs (simulate NAT/egress churn)
3) Observe model selection in response metadata: some requests go to canary variant (redwood-3b-quant), others go to baseline (redwood-3b-v1) despite tenant pin expected to hold
4) Reproduce more consistently by toggling X-Forwarded-For header between original IP and a proxied IP; model selection changes correlate with header surface change

investigation_notes: Initial triage: customer reports mixed outputs; metrics show session-level variance in model selection correlated with changes to client IP observed at the edge.
Hypothesis A: Pin key derivation includes client_ip shard (by legacy design) and BrightFields' egress NAT churn changed client_ip surface, causing different pin hashes and split routing.

Hypothesis B: Edge proxy normalizes X-Forwarded-For / Forwarded header and sometimes rewrites to internal egress IP under high concurrency; this rewriting is intermittent and not reflected in pin cache TTL logic, producing brief split-pinning windows.
Checked orchestrator snapshot: canary slices configured to use 'cohort_key=client_ip_hash' for staged promote (confirmed), which increases sensitivity to XFF changes.

Confirmed TTLs: pin TTL set at 12 hours for dedicated tenants; however pin assignment depends on hash computed at request time, so different client_ip values produce distinct pin entries instead of reusing the canonical tenant pin.
Edge logs show two different client_shard values for consecutive requests from same session where only XFF changed — supports Hypothesis A+B.
No evidence of control-plane rollback or orchestrator epoch bump during the window; no autoscaler events correlated.

Customer provided sample pcap showing NAT churn frequency ~3s between connections during their internal deploy; this is higher than typical and explains high rate of pin splitting for their traffic pattern.

comments: Sofia Martinez (Support): Added initial reproducer and customer-provided traces. Asked SRE to triage.
Ethan Zhang (SRE): Reproduced locally by toggling X-Forwarded-For -> confirmed model selection changed when client_ip_hash changed. Marking as Sev1 due to customer eval regressions.
Dev (Anjali Rao): Confirmed orchestrator uses cohort_key=client_ip_hash for BrightFields tenant; will prioritize tenant-scoped override to use tenant_cookie when available. Working on PR.
Customer (BrightFields - ops@brightfields): We can set explicit model param for now but need a permanent fix; our infra team will reduce NAT churn as stop-gap.
proposed_actions: P0 workaround: Instruct customer to provide explicit 'x-redwood-model: redwood-3b-quant' header or pass model parameter on critical evaluation requests (applies immediately)
Short-term mitigation: Deploy edge canonicalization for Forwarded/X-Forwarded-For header priority (already rolling to subset of edge-hosts) to reduce IP churn surface visibility to routing layer
Medium-term fix: Change canary cohort_key default to prefer tenant_cookie > client_ip_hash and make cohort_key configurable per-tenant in orchestration UI/tenant profile
Postmortem action: Update docs and runbook for tenant guidance on when to use explicit model parameter vs. rely on pinning when customer egress IPs may vary frequently
resolution: Partial mitigations applied: edge canonicalization rolled to 30% of edge fleet and customer instructed to use explicit model header for evaluation traffic. Orchestrator PR #1448 opened to make cohort key configurable and prefer tenant_cookie; target rollout for medium-term fix in next week. Customer reported visible reduction in split responses after edge change. Ticket remains In Progress until orchestrator change is deployed and verified across BrightFields traffic.
